brief: Found by R10-SETPOINT-BOOST's demand analysis. The COP model keys only on outdoor temperature and the tank/weather-curve flow; it has no power (part-load) dependence and no burst term. So the planner cannot weigh tvofi's hypotheses (2026-10-19): power near the floor is suboptimal under price swings, and a short high-power burst does not raise the flow temperature enough to hurt COP much. Measure first on synthetic installs: COP vs compressor power at a fixed lift, and the flow-temperature rise during a short burst. Add a model term only if the measured effect is material, with controls: a flat-price null, a no-term null that keeps plans byte-identical, and mutation. Must work without a heat meter.
